purpose: Ketoconazole cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as athlete's foot, jock itch, ringworm, and yeast infections of the skin. It can also help with a condition called tinea versicolor, which causes discolored patches on the skin. Your doctor may also recommend it for dandruff or seborrheic dermatitis in some cases.
how_it_works: Ketoconazole works by attacking the outer wall of the fungus, called the cell membrane. It blocks a substance the fungus needs to keep its cell wall strong and intact. Without that protection, the fungal cells break down and die, clearing up your infection.
common_side_effects: Some people may notice mild skin irritation, redness, itching, or a burning or stinging feeling where the cream is applied. These reactions are usually mild and tend to go away as your skin adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do not use this cream near your eyes, mouth, or inside your nose. If you develop severe irritation, a rash, or signs of an allergic reaction like swelling or trouble breathing, stop using it and contact your doctor right away. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have any known allergies to antifungal medications. Only use it on your skin — do not swallow it.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer of the cream to the affected skin area once or twice daily, as directed by your doctor. Gently rub it in and wash your hands after applying. Most treatments last 2 to 6 weeks depending on the type of infection. Keep using it for the full recommended time even if your skin looks better early, to make sure the infection is fully gone.
